## Summary

The 68080 fuses certain pairs (and one triple) of instructions into a single 64-bit or 3-operand instruction.

## Details

- Fuse can combine two instructions by using 64bit or 3 operand.
- Treated by the core as a single instruction.
- The result is a 32bit register update or 64bit memory update.

### Two-instruction fuses

| Instruction 1 | Instruction 2 | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| `move.l (an)+,(am)+` | `move.l (an)+,(am)+` | quad move |
| `move.l (an)+,dn` | `move.l (an)+,dm` | quad move |
| `move.l dn,(an)+` | `move.l dm,(an)+` | quad move |
| `clr.l (an)+` | `clr.l (an)+` | quad clr |
| `move.l dn,dm` | `not.b/w/l dm` | & neg, addq, subq |
| `move.l dn,dm` | `addi.l #,dm` | & subi |
| `move.l dn,dm` | `add.b/w/l dx,dm` | & sub, and, or, eor |
| `move.l dn,dm` | `bchg dx,dm` | & bset, bclr |
| `moveq #,dn` | `and.(b/w/l) dx,dn` | & or |
| `move.l dn,dm` | `andi.w #,dm` |  |
|  |  | all shifters exept rox(r/l) |
| `move.l dn,dm` | `asr.b/w/l #im,dm` | & as, ls, ro(r/l) |
| `move.l dn,dm` | `asr.b/w/l dx,dm` | & as, ls, ro(r/l) |
| `moveq #,dn` | `move.b (ea),dn` | movz.b (ea),dn |
| `moveq #,dn` | `move.w (ea),dn` | movz.w (ea),dn |
| `move.l (ea),dn` | `extb.l dn` | & swap |
| `move.w (ea),dn` | `ext.l dn` | movs.w (ea),dn |
| `ext.w dn` | `ext.l dn` | extb.l |
| `subq.l #1,dn` | `bne.s/s+/w` | almost dbra |
| `fmove.x fpn,fpm` | `fmul.x fpx,fpm` | fmul fpn,fpx,fpm |
| `fmove.x fpn,fpm` | `fadd.x fpx,fpm` | fadd fpn,fpx,fpm |

### Three-instruction fuses

| Instruction 1 | Instruction 2 | Instruction 3 | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| `move.l dm,dn` | `ext.w dn` | `ext.l dn` |  |

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 do not fuse instructions.

## Do / Don't

- DO write fusable pairs back to back, for example two `move.l (an)+,(am)+` for a quad move.
